_notes.title: The timeline's name, shown at the top and at the left of the printed strip.
_notes.subtitle: One line under the title. Optional; an empty string leaves it out.
_notes.eras: The layered bands. Each has a label, from and to dates, and a color: red, orange, gold, green, teal, blue, violet, or rose (each theme draws them in its own tones), or a #rrggbb color. Eras that overlap sit in separate layers, in the order listed.
_notes.events: The pins. Each has a date and a label; text, image, and era are optional. An image is a path beside this file (or a picture in the app's sample folder) and is copied into the page. An era names one of the eras by its label; left out, the event takes the era its date falls in.
_notes.dates: Every date is a year (1911), a month (1911-05), or a day (1911-05-02). A year before the common era starts with a minus sign: -500 is 500 BCE.
_notes.start: The date at the start of the first view.
_notes.end: The date at the end of the first view.
_notes.orientation: auto (across on a wide screen, down on a tall one), horizontal, or vertical.
_notes.theme: parchment (light), museum (dark), or auto (parchment in a light color scheme, museum in a dark one).
_notes.autoplay: true opens the page on the story walk, easing from event to event until the person touches the timeline; false opens it still.

title: The Lindgren Family
subtitle: Five generations, from a Småland farm to a Seattle backyard

events.label: Anders is born in Vislanda
events.text: Anders Lindgren, the second son of a tenant farmer, is born in the red cottage at the edge of the Vislanda birch wood. The parish book spells the name three different ways in his first ten years.

events.label: Kristina Persdotter is born
events.text: Kristina grows up two farms over and walks to the same church every Sunday. She will outlive Anders by eleven years.

events.label: The famine years
events.text: Three wet summers in a row ruin the harvest across Småland. Neighbors leave for America by the cartload; the Lindgrens stay and eat bark bread through the winter of 1868.

events.label: A Midsummer wedding
events.text: Anders and Kristina marry on Midsummer Eve, under a maypole the whole village helped raise. The wedding crown is borrowed from the church.

events.label: Erik is born
events.text: The third of five children, and the only one who will leave.

events.label: Erik apprenticed to a baker
events.text: At fourteen Erik walks to Växjö to sleep above the Hultman bakery and learn rye, cardamom, and how to get up at three.

events.label: Erik meets Margit Olsson
events.text: Margit serves coffee at the Boxing Day dance in Växjö. Erik buys four cups he does not drink.

events.label: Erik and Margit marry
events.text: A small wedding in the Växjö cathedral, with two tickets to America already paid for.

events.label: They leave Göteborg
events.text: Erik and Margit board the Ariadne at Göteborg with one trunk, a sourdough starter in a crock, and Kristina's Bible.

events.label: Train from Hull to Liverpool
events.text: The North Sea crossing ends at Hull; a sealed emigrant train takes them across England in a single day.

events.label: Sailing from Liverpool
events.text: Steerage on a White Star liner: nine days, two storms, and a cabin shared with a family from Kalmar.

events.label: Ellis Island
events.text: Inspected, chalk-marked, and passed in under four hours. Margit keeps the landing card for the rest of her life.

events.label: Arriving in Saint Paul
events.text: Erik's cousin meets the train at Union Depot and walks them to a room on the East Side.

events.label: Lindgren's Bakery opens
events.text: A storefront on Payne Avenue with one oven and Margit at the counter. The cardamom buns sell out by nine.

events.label: Anders dies in Vislanda
events.text: The letter takes five weeks to arrive. Erik closes the bakery for a day, the only day it closes that year.

events.label: Ruth is born above the bakery
events.text: Erik and Margit's only daughter, born in the apartment over the ovens, and warm, she says, ever since.

events.label: Ruth marries Tom Haugen
events.text: Tom is a lineman for Northern States Power. The cake is seven layers, and Erik will not let anyone else bake it.

events.label: The landing, on the bakery's TV
events.text: Half of Payne Avenue crowds into the bakery to watch the landing on the set above the bread racks.

events.label: Erik dies; Margit keeps baking
events.text: Margit runs the bakery for eight more years with Ruth on Saturdays.

events.label: Lena is born
events.text: Ruth and Tom's second child, named for Margit's sister.

events.label: The bakery is sold
events.text: The Nguyen family buys the bakery and keeps the sign. They still sell cardamom buns on Saturdays.

events.label: Lena drives west to Seattle
events.text: Three days in a Datsun with a box of Margit's recipe cards on the passenger seat.

events.label: Lena marries Jonas Berg
events.text: A ferry wedding on the way to Bainbridge Island. Jonas's family is from Göteborg, which nobody believes at first.

events.label: The twins, Elsa and Nils
events.text: Born on Erik's birthday, ninety years later.

events.label: Back to Vislanda
events.text: Lena takes the twins to see the red cottage. It is a summer house now, and the owners invite them in for coffee.

events.label: Ruth dies at 79
events.text: Her recipe box goes to Elsa, who is the only one who can read the handwriting.

events.label: Midsummer reunion
events.text: Forty-one Lindgrens, Haugens, and Bergs in one Seattle backyard, a maypole made from a curtain rod, and cardamom buns from the Nguyens, flown in.
